falsi.subtitle: A Heart Tempered into a Blade
falsi.description: She carried out the Thirteenth Legion's orders without ever letting anyone read what she made of them. When nothing was left to serve, she walked away alone, two blades and two pistols for an inheritance.
falsi.name: Falsi

ada.subtitle: The Lone Bunny of Paradise
ada.description: Two sets of memories live behind her smile: a homeland torn apart by war, and a paradise that may never have existed. She walks between them, never saying which one is hers.
ada.name: Ada

flora.subtitle: Rebel Bloom
flora.description: Beneath petals of onyx simmers a slow wrath. Each thorn marks a broken oath; each blossom, a deferred reckoning. Night opens to her passage like a garden someone forgot to lock.

hilda.subtitle: Crimson Apron
hilda.description: Beneath the spotless linens of a maid in service to a noble house sleep the tools of a fidelity sharper than stone. When silence falls, her blades do the speaking.
hilda.name: Hilda

nvzhu02.subtitle: Shadow's Reflection
nvzhu02.description: The other side of fate: where the light fades, another voice rises. She walks the abyss wearing the same face, but different oaths — and this time she chooses not to turn back.
nvzhu02.name: Female Protagonist

nanzhu02.subtitle: Echo in Ink
nanzhu02.description: What you think you left behind sometimes returns, dressed as yourself. Beneath the mantle of shadow rest unkept promises, and a quiet step that no longer asks for forgiveness.
nanzhu02.name: Male Protagonist

privacy.title: Privacy & terms
privacy.intro: Applies to Discord sign-in and the community build builder.
privacy.data1: Discord ID, nickname and avatar (to identify you as an author).
privacy.data2: Your Discord email, if you allow it at sign-in.
privacy.data3: The builds, drafts and votes you create on the site.
privacy.dataNote: This account data is not used for advertising and is not sold. Audience measurement is described separately below.
privacy.purposeText: This data is only used to run accounts and build sharing (authentication, attributing a build to its author, votes, moderation). It is kept as long as your account exists and is deleted when you delete your account.
privacy.analyticsText: We use Sarutobi, a self-hosted solution, to measure pages and journeys, sources and campaigns, approximate country, device and browser, Web Vitals, redacted JavaScript errors and selected product actions. A pseudonymous session identifier is used; when you are signed in, it may be linked to your internal account ID. No email, password, nickname, search, build content or form value is sent. Retention depends on the project configuration.
privacy.optOutText: Measurement starts on your first visit, without a banner. You can object at any time; the choice is kept in this browser.
privacy.optOutActive: Audience measurement is active in this browser.
privacy.optOutDisabled: Audience measurement is disabled in this browser.
privacy.optOutNote: This setting is stored locally: it does not follow your account and must be set again in another browser or after clearing site data.
privacy.rightsText: At any time you can view your data, edit or delete your builds, and permanently delete your account (together with all your builds, drafts and votes) from your profile. Deletion is immediate and irreversible.
privacy.ugc1: You remain responsible for the builds and names you publish.
privacy.ugc2: Build names and notes must not contain hateful speech, harassment, illegal content or spam.
privacy.ugc3: A build can be reported by the community; an administrator may hide or delete it, and ban an account in case of repeated abuse.
privacy.ugc4: By publishing a build, you agree that it is displayed publicly on the site with your Discord nickname and avatar.
privacy.contactText: For any question about your data or the removal of content, use the <link>contact</link> page.

itemsAbout.title: How Demon Wedges work
itemsAbout.intro: In game, Demon Wedges may also appear under the technical name <mod>MOD</mod> in some data. This page explains the key fields used across the site: level, affinity, tolerance, dynamic effects and asset mapping.
itemsAbout.showcaseDescription: Examples of Demon Wedge icons used in the grid and the detail page. The goal is to recognise a Demon Wedge at a glance.
itemsAbout.readStep1Text: Lets you identify the Demon Wedge in the grid.
itemsAbout.readStep2Text: The symbol next to the name shows the Demon Wedge affinity type.
itemsAbout.readStep3Text: The detail slider changes the dynamic values #1, #2, #3.
itemsAbout.structureItem1: Every Demon Wedge has a name, a description, a rarity, an affinity and a max level.
itemsAbout.structureItem2: The name shown in game is <c>Demon Wedge</c>. <c>MOD</c> remains mostly a technical term used in some internal data.
itemsAbout.structureItem3: Texts (name, description, passive effects) change with the selected language.
itemsAbout.structureItem4: The site exposes this info as JSON so you can filter, compare languages and open details.
itemsAbout.affinityDescription: The detail sheet combines several visual cues: polarity symbol, elemental affinity and compatibility tags for the character/weapon type.
itemsAbout.levelsText: The values <c>#1</c>, <c>#2</c>, etc. change with the Demon Wedge level. The slider on the detail page applies those values from the growth table and shows the effect at the chosen level.
itemsAbout.toleranceText: The displayed tolerance scales with level. The formula exposed in the data is:
itemsAbout.toleranceNote: The site pre-computes per-level values and stores them in <c>tolerance.valuesByLevel</c>.
itemsAbout.multilangText: On the grid: you can show several languages at once to compare names. On the detail: a single language can be picked and shared through the URL.
itemsAbout.multilangNote: The languages currently available depend on the dataset loaded for the category.
itemsAbout.displayItem1: General Demon Wedge info (name, rarity, function, description)
itemsAbout.displayItem5: Search, filters, favourites and pagination for navigation
itemsAbout.quickTitle: Reading a Demon Wedge at a glance on the site
itemsAbout.quickText: The visual path is always the same: identify the icon, check the affinity, then adjust the level to see the dynamic effects.
itemsAbout.nextText: Use the grid to filter and compare quickly, then open an item to see its dynamic values, its per-level tolerance and its affinity.
itemsAbout.genericText: This category is ready to host a detailed explanatory page. The system is already in place to add the rules, formulas and visuals specific to each new item family.
itemsAbout.trackIntro: Every slot carries a track. Applying a Track-Shift Module aligns that track with the polarity of the piece sitting there, and halves its tolerance cost.
itemsAbout.trackBadgeCost: The number: the slot's tolerance cost.
itemsAbout.trackBadgeGlyph: The glyph: the current track — flame 1, crescent 2, diamond 3, circle 4.
itemsAbout.trackBadgeCrown: The crown: a module is applied to this slot.
itemsAbout.trackBadgeGreen: A green badge means a reduced cost, so an aligned track. White means full price.
itemsAbout.trackRule: A track that is set always equals the polarity of its piece. A misalignment is never a tactical choice: it takes the cost from half to one and a half times.
itemsAbout.trackCostRule: Aligned track: cost ÷ 2. Misaligned track: cost × 1.5. No module: full cost.
itemsAbout.centerIntro: The core is a slot like any other — the armory numbers it 09 — and it takes a Track-Shift Module exactly like the eight around it.
itemsAbout.centerAffinity: It is what gives the build its affinity: the label shown always derives from it, it is never picked separately.
itemsAbout.centerTiers: Two families of cores coexist, and both are legitimate: the generic 3★ ones, with no element, often kept into the endgame, and the elemental 4★ and 5★ ones.
itemsAbout.stackIntro: As a rule, one piece per family across the whole wheel.
itemsAbout.stackRule: Only one family escapes that rule, Covenanter's: its pieces stack once upgraded to +5.
itemsAbout.stackTrap: A trap: 828 pieces out of 829 share the same icon. Two slots that look identical are not necessarily duplicates — compare the names.
itemsAbout.captionBoard: The armory screen: eight slots around the core, tolerance gauge on top.
itemsAbout.captionApply: The game offering to apply a module to the selected slot.
itemsAbout.captionStacking: The stacking note on a Covenanter's piece.
itemsAbout.metaModsDescription: Understand how Demon Wedges work: levels, affinity, tolerance, translations and reading the effects.

calamityGuide.metaDescription: How to unlock them, the Calamity Furnace, smelting levels, Potentials and materials: everything needed to build a Calamity Weapon in Duet Night Abyss.
calamityGuide.title: Building a Calamity Weapon
calamityGuide.intro: A Calamity Weapon does not level like any other. It swaps ordinary smelting for Calamity Smelting, a six-step path that opens Potentials — weapon-specific effects that only fire in the hands of a character proficient with that weapon type. This guide covers unlocking, the Furnace, the Potential tree and the materials to stockpile.
calamityGuide.imageOverview: The Calamity Smelting screen: the weapon's Potential tree, your progress and the current cap.
calamityGuide.imageUnlock: The quest that unlocks Calamity Weapons, or the forge screen.
calamityGuide.imageFurnace: The Calamity Furnace, shared by every weapon you own.
calamityGuide.imagePotential: A selected Potential: its effect on the right, and the weapon-proficiency rule restated at the bottom.
calamityGuide.rulesTitle: Three rules to know going in
calamityGuide.ruleDamageTitle: An upgrade path of its own
calamityGuide.ruleDamageBody: Calamity Weapons have their own progression and their own effects. Every hit builds Calamity; once the gauge fills, it empties at once to trigger the weapon's signature effect.
calamityGuide.ruleOneBody: The game is explicit: a character can equip only one Calamity Weapon at a time. Two characters can each carry one, but you never stack two on the same character.
calamityGuide.ruleProficiencyBody: Potentials only take effect if the weapon type matches the character's proficiency. A Calamity polearm in the hands of someone who does not wield polearms is still a weapon, but its tree does nothing.
calamityGuide.obtainStep1Body: A dedicated quest opens the whole system once your trial rank is high enough. It expects endgame progress and a stock of faction emblems handed in; in return it leaves you the first weapon blueprint.
calamityGuide.obtainStep2Body: The weapon is crafted at the forge from prototypes of that specific weapon, forging insights of the right type, and coin. Crafting takes hours, so start it before heading back out.
calamityGuide.obtainStep3Body: Prototypes come from outside the forge: the Immersive Theatre exchange shop, and Abyssal Expeditions, where enemies already start at very high levels. This is the real bottleneck.
calamityGuide.furnaceBody: The Furnace is a global level shared by every Calamity Weapon you own. It rises by completing Furnace level tasks, not by playing one particular weapon.
calamityGuide.furnaceGateBody: Its level sets the smelting level cap for all your Calamity Weapons. In other words: hoarding materials achieves nothing until the Furnace reaches the tier you want — and once it does, it opens that tier for every weapon at once. The tasks that raise it are taken from Luno the blacksmith, at the Sanctuary.
calamityGuide.furnaceFreeNode: Worth knowing: once a smelting level is unlocked, the first Potential you pick at that level costs no materials. The second one does.
calamityGuide.potentialBody: Every Calamity Weapon has its own tree: ten Potentials spread across six tiers, from smelting level 0 to level V. Raising the smelting level opens the matching tier; what you unlock inside it is your call.
calamityGuide.potentialRuleShape: Tiers 0 and V hold a single Potential; tiers I to IV hold two, usually one offensive branch and one utility branch.
calamityGuide.potentialRuleFree: The first Potential unlocked at a tier is free. The second costs materials but stays available — there is no permanent choice to regret.
calamityGuide.potentialRuleChain: A Potential requires its predecessor to be unlocked and the matching smelting level to be reached. Tiers cannot be skipped.
calamityGuide.potentialSeeSheet: The full tree, tier by tier, with each Potential's effect and cost, lives on each weapon's own page.
calamityGuide.materialsBody: Almost everything comes from Abyssal missions. They come in two modes, both labelled “Calamity Weapon materials”, and start with an Abyssal Compass.
calamityGuide.costTitle: Cost of each level, weapon by weapon
calamityGuide.costBody: The costs below are the game's own, read straight from its tables. They show what to gather to move from one smelting level to the next.
calamityGuide.costUnavailable: This weapon's costs are not filled in yet on the game's side.
calamityGuide.nextBody: A finished Calamity Weapon does not replace a build, it slots into one. The weapon's Demon Wedges, its affinity and its track still need work for the Potentials to actually pay off.
calamityGuide.imagePotentialCost: A Potential's cost, shown as owned / required.
calamityGuide.imageMissions: The two Abyssal missions, both labelled “Calamity Weapon materials”.
calamityGuide.imageEmblemTooltip: An emblem's tooltip states how to obtain it: which mission, and which enemies to target.
legendFurnace: The Furnace level, shared by all your Calamity Weapons.
What the tier opens: the smelting level cap.
Furnace level tasks, picked up from Luno the blacksmith at the Sanctuary.
legendPotentialCost: The first Potential unlocked at a tier costs no materials.
The second one does: each tile shows what you hold against what it needs.
legendExpedition: The targeted rare reward: this is where you aim at a specific prototype.
The enemies' attribute, chosen before entering.
An Abyssal Compass is required to start the mission.
legendDefense: Difficulty tiers, from level 40 to level 80.
calamityGuide.potentialCostBody: The right-hand panel shows the selected Potential's cost, as owned over required. A red figure marks what you are still short of.
calamityGuide.potentialOrderBody: Since the first pick at each tier is free, order matters: take the one whose materials you lack the most first, and pay for the other later.
calamityGuide.missionsBody: Expedition and Defence drop different materials. The game tells you which to run: every material's tooltip carries an “Obtained from” line naming the mission and the enemies.
calamityGuide.compassBody: The Abyssal Compass is picked at launch: the higher its level, the better the rewards. It levels up by clearing more rounds, and in a party only the leader spends one.
calamityGuide.emblemsBody: Each emblem drops from one specific faction's enemies, in one specific mission. Farming is targeted: there is no point hoping for an Emblem of Harmony anywhere but on Huaxu enemies.
calamityGuide.crystalsBody: Crystals are targeted at the mission's launch screen. You pick the rare reward you want and the enemies' attribute, which makes farming a specific elemental crystal predictable.
calamityGuide.provisionalNotice: Unscheduled weapon: its name and displayed type still come from a work-in-progress entry in the game data and will change at release. Its art, however, already ships with the game.
calamityGuide.pathBody: Since the first Potential at each tier is free, the question is not “which branch” but “which one do I take for free, four times”. The tiers are not equal: the first decides everything, the rest follow your playstyle.
pathTiers: Tier I — the calamity source. The decisive pick: a source the character never triggers is a dead Potential.
Tier II — a raw stat. Skill Intensity if the damage comes from skills, ATK if it comes from the weapon.
Tier III — a conditional amplifier. Charged versus normal attacks, summoning versus consuming: take the condition you meet.
Tier IV — the second stat. Same reading as tier II, with what is left.
pathWeapons: Perpetual Strife is built on summons: familiars generate calamity and inherit your attributes.
Sovereign Ember amplifies the melee consonance weapon, from charged attacks to crit rate.
Sanguine Plume revolves around HP and Elemental Disorder, ending on Max HP +300%.
Thorned Requiem turns Combo points into [Extinction], harder and harder.
calamityGuide.pathSeeCharacter: The recommended order for a given character is shown on their page, under the weapon, right on the tree.

genimonGuide.ascensionBody: Ascension happens at levels 20, 40 and 60, then once more with no level requirement. Each one asks for a Geniemon of the same species — any of its variants — and one Yum-Yum Milk.
genimonGuide.ascensionOpensSlots: Every ascension opens a Trait slot. It is the only way to get one: an ordinary variant ends with three, a shining variant with four.
genimonGuide.categoryHint_battle: Everything about skills, crits and Geniemon Support.
genimonGuide.categoryHint_world: Outside combat: pickup, loot, fishing, mechanisms.
genimonGuide.fusionBody: A Trait exists in three rarities. Three identical copies of one rarity give one of the rarity above, so nine blue Traits are needed for a single gold one.
genimonGuide.fusionChainNote: three at each step, so nine blues for one gold
genimonGuide.imageAscension: Ascension, and the step it opens.
genimonGuide.imageLevelUp: Geniemon Upgrade: on the left what you can feed it, on the right the five slots and the experience gained.
genimonGuide.imageOverview: A Geniemon's page: level, rarity and passive.
genimonGuide.imageTraitSlots: The spheres are the slots. A full one holds a Trait, an empty one waits, a locked one needs an ascension.
genimonGuide.intro: An equipped Geniemon grants a passive bonus to the whole party, plus up to four Traits stacked on top. Raising one is therefore two jobs: the creature itself, and the Traits it carries.
genimonGuide.listBody: The four categories below are the game's own, each with its glyph. The colour carries the rarity: blue, purple, gold. The glyphs in front of a Trait are the rarities it comes in.
genimonGuide.nextBody: The individual pages give each Geniemon in detail: its passive, its values and its variants.
genimonGuide.passiveBody: Each species carries its own passive, benefiting the main character and Combat Partners alike. Most raise one element's ATK; the rarer ones also boost the stats given by certain Demon Wedges, or affect exploration and movement.
genimonGuide.passiveShiny: Variants of the same species share exactly the same passive and the same values. What separates them is the number of Trait slots — and that is where the real gap lies.
genimonGuide.raiseBody: A Geniemon goes up to level 60. Feed it Yum, Yum-Yum and Yum-Yum-Yum Creams, or other Geniemons used as material — a consumed Geniemon returns the experience it had gathered itself.
raiseSteps: Yum, Yum-Yum and Yum-Yum-Yum Creams grant experience, from the least to the most generous.
A Geniemon used as material returns its experience: the ones you will never equip are never wasted.
The level is capped at each ascension step. Without ascending, gathered experience goes nowhere.
genimonGuide.title: Raising a Geniemon
genimonGuide.traitsActiveInactive: Traits are harvested from inactive Geniemons, the ones you do not send into battle. An inactive Geniemon is therefore never useless: it is a reserve of Traits for the ones you actually play.
genimonGuide.traitsBody: A Trait is a bonus grafted into a slot opened by ascension. It adds to the species passive rather than replacing it, so a single Geniemon can stack its passive and up to four Traits.
genimonGuide.flowCaption: An inactive Geniemon is a reservoir: its Traits go to the one you take into battle. The fourth slot exists only on a shining variant.
genimonGuide.listValueNote: The ellipsis stands in for a number: it rises with the Trait's rarity, and the game only shows it on the piece itself.
genimonGuide.trainingBody: A Trait is not rolled, it is passed on. Geniemon Training takes a Trait held by an inactive Geniemon and gives it to an active one, and the Trait you pick replaces whatever occupied the slot. That is what inactive Geniemons are for, the ones you never take into battle.
genimonGuide.trainingLevel: A Trait's level is raised separately, through Raise. A slot can also be locked so it is not overwritten by mistake, and the Trait Compendium does this automatically for the Traits you mark.
genimonGuide.imageTraining: Geniemon Training: passing a Trait from an inactive Geniemon to an active one.
genimonGuide.goldOnlyNote: Seven Traits exist only in gold and therefore cannot be reached by merging: they have to be found as they are.
genimonGuide.variantShinyTell: Same species, same passive, same values. The shining one is known by its aura and opens a fourth Trait slot: that is the whole difference, and it is a large one.
genimonGuide.shopBody: Bounty Commissions now have their own exchange, Bounty Rewards, with a Geniemon tab. Two currencies follow one another there: the first is earned on commissions, the second only comes out of what the first paid for.
shopSteps: Chase and Showdown commissions pay out A Geniemon's Ballad Ⅰ.
Ballad Ⅰ buys Surprise Chests: one random Geniemon, active or inactive, plus A Geniemon's Ballad Ⅱ.
Ballad Ⅱ buys the Selection Chests, where you choose for yourself. One per period, restocked roughly every three weeks.
genimonGuide.shopGoldTraits: This is where the seven gold Traits come from. The Inactive Geniemon Selection Chest lets you take a Geniemon carrying Tenacious, Deft, At Peace, Disciplined, Desirous, Fleeing or Veteran — exactly the seven that merging cannot reach.
genimonGuide.imageShopPath: The exchange opens from Bounty Commissions.
genimonGuide.imageShopChests: The four chests, and the currency each one asks for.
genimonGuide.imageShopSelection: A selection chest states what it lets you choose.
